source_text: Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo adque argumentis opus non est. probatio est ad fidem facilis conpendio ueritatis. loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus et super istam petram aedificabo ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non uincent eam. dabo tibi claues regni caelorum: et quae ligaueris super terram erunt ligata et in caelis, et quaecumque solueris super terram erunt soluta et in caelis. super unum aedificat ecclesiam, et quamuis apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat: sicut u t misit me pater et ego mitto uos. accipite Spiritum sanctum: si cuius remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi: si cuius tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen ut unitatem manifestaret, unitatis eiusdem originem ab uno incipientem. sua auctoritate disposuit. hoc erant utique et ceteri apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, ut ecclesia Christi una monstretur. quam unam ecclesiam etiam in cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: una est columbamea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genetrici suae. hanc ecclesiae unitatem qui non tenet tenere se fidem credit? qui ecclesiae renititur et resistit in ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes uocationis uestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus.
thought_title: The Church's unity founded on Peter
orientation: Cyprian is arguing that the Church's unity is easily proved from Christ's words to Peter and from Scripture, so no long argument is needed.
pass_a_gloss: Which [things] if anyone should consider and examine, [there] is not need [of] long treatise and [of] arguments. proof is easy for faith by [the] compendium of truth. [The] Lord speaks to Peter: I say to you, he says, that you are Peter and upon this rock I will build my church, and [the] gates of [the] underworld will not overcome it. I will give to you [the] keys of [the] kingdom of [the] heavens: and which [things] you will have bound upon [the] earth will be bound also in [the] heavens, and whatever [things] you will have loosed upon [the] earth will be loosed also in [the] heavens. upon one he builds [the] church, and although to all [the] apostles after his resurrection he grants equal power and says: just as [the] father sent me also I send you. receive [the] Holy Spirit: if of anyone you will have forgiven sins, they will be forgiven to him: if of anyone you will have retained [them], they will be retained, nevertheless that he might make manifest [the] unity, [the] origin of [the] same unity beginning from one. by his authority he arranged [it]. this certainly were also [the] other apostles what Peter was, endowed with equal sharing both of honor and of power, but [the] beginning proceeds from unity, that [the] church of Christ [might be] shown [as] one. which one church also in [the] song of songs [the] Holy Spirit from [the] person of [the] Lord designates and says: one is my dove, my perfect [one], one [she is] to her mother, chosen to her parent. this unity of [the] church [he] who does not hold believes [that] he holds [the] faith? [he] who opposes [the] church and resists trusts [that] he is in [the] church? when also [the] blessed apostle Paul teaches this same [thing] and shows [the] sacrament of unity saying: one body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the demonstrative and noun; preserves the wordplay with Petrus/petram.
Literal translation of inferorum as underworld, matching the Old Latin source and avoiding modern 'hell' which could import later theological nuance.
Glossary requires 'sacred sign' for sacramentum; keeps the literal sense of a sign that reveals unity.

choices.term: una est columba mea, perfecta mea
choices.english: one is my dove, my perfect one
choices.why: Literal word order and possessive adjectives preserved; 'perfect one' renders the feminine adjective substantively.
rejected: my dove is one, my perfect one
one is my dove, my flawless one

choices.term: pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis
choices.english: endowed with equal sharing both of honor and of power
choices.why: Literal rendering of pari consortio as 'equal sharing' and the double genitive with et...et as 'both...and'.
rejected: endowed with equal partnership of honor and power
sharing equally in honor and power

choices.why: Literal translation of proficiscitur as 'proceeds' and ab unitate as 'from unity', preserving the spatial metaphor.

pass_b_english: If anyone considers and examines these things, there is no need for a long treatment or arguments. The proof is easy for faith, by a summary of the truth. The Lord says to Peter: "I tell you, you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of the underworld will not overcome it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matthew 16:18-19). He builds the Church upon one man. And although after his resurrection he grants equal power to all the apostles and says: "As the Father sent me, I also send you. Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven; if you retain anyone's sins, they are retained" (John 20:21-23), yet to make unity manifest, he arranged by his own authority that the origin of this same unity should begin from one. Certainly the other apostles were what Peter was, endowed with equal sharing both of honor and of power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, so that the Church of Christ may be shown to be one. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord, and says: "One is my dove, my perfect one; one is she to her mother, chosen to her who bore her" (Song of Songs 6:9). Does someone who does not hold this unity of the Church believe that he holds the faith? Does someone who opposes and resists the Church trust that he is in the Church? For the blessed apostle Paul also teaches this same thing and shows the sacred sign of unity, saying: "One body and one Spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God" (Ephesians 4:4-6).

last_rejected.why: English reverses speakers: source has Spirit speaking in person of Lord, not Lord speaking.
last_rejected.fix: The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, from the Lord's person, saying
last_rejected.ruling: English 'speaking in the person of the Lord' modifies Spiritus sanctus; no reversal of speakers, just ambiguous syntax.

last_rejected.quote: the proof is easy for faith, by a summary of the truth
last_rejected.source_quote: probatio est ad fidem facilis conpendio ueritatis
last_rejected.why: Latin 'ad fidem' means 'to produce belief/conviction', not 'for faith'.
last_rejected.fix: the proof to convince is easy, through a summary of the truth
last_rejected.ruling: 'ad fidem facilis' = easy for faith/to produce belief; both renderings fall within normal range of meaning.

last_rejected.why: Latin means 'the beginning starts from unity', not 'proceeds from unity'; 'proficiscitur' here = begins/sets out.
last_rejected.ruling: 'proficiscitur' = proceeds/sets out/begins; 'proceeds from' is within normal range, not a meaning change.
